title: The Wolves, the Sheep, and the Ram
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: The Wolves sent a deputation to the Sheep with proposals for a lasting peace between them, on condition of their giving up the sheep-dogs to instant death. The foolish Sheep agreed to the terms; but an old Ram, whose years had brought him wisdom, interfered and said, "How can we expect to live at peace with you? Why, even with the dogs at hand to protect us, we are never secure from your murderous attacks!"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Wolves send to the Sheep?
options: A deputation with proposals for a lasting peace

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what condition did the Wolves attach to their peace proposal?
options: That the Sheep move to new pastures
That the Sheep pay a yearly tribute
That the Sheep never graze near the forest
That the Sheep give up the sheep-dogs to instant death

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Sheep respond to the Wolves' terms?
options: They foolishly agreed to the terms
They asked the Ram to decide for them

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who spoke up against the agreement?
As the passage uses it, what does "deputation" mean in "sent a deputation to the Sheep"?
options: A group sent to represent others

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "secure" mean in "we are never secure from your murderous attacks"?
Based on the passage, why does the Ram doubt the Wolves' peace proposal?
options: He believes the Wolves are too weak to attack anyone
He reasons that if the Wolves still attack even with the dogs present, losing the dogs would only make things worse
He thinks the Sheep already have more protection than they need
He notices the Wolves have never lied before

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Peace agreements are always beneficial to both sides
Old age always brings better judgment than youth
One should be wary of an enemy's peace offer that requires giving up one's own protection
Dogs are more dangerous than wolves

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Ram say about the Sheep's safety even with the dogs present?
options: They are safe only at night
They are safe only in winter
They are never secure from the Wolves' murderous attacks

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is said to have given the Ram his wisdom?
According to the passage, what fate awaited the sheep-dogs under the Wolves' proposed terms?
As the passage uses it, what does "murderous" mean in "your murderous attacks"?
Based on the passage, what does calling the Sheep "foolish" for agreeing suggest about them compared to the Ram?
options: The Sheep are more experienced negotiators than the Ram
The Sheep are quicker to trust the Wolves than the more cautious, experienced Ram
The Sheep and the Ram share exactly the same judgment
The Sheep secretly agree with the Wolves' goals

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Wolves and the Sheep and Ram become lasting allies
The Ram convinces the Wolves to give up hunting
The Wolves offer peace if the Sheep give up their guard dogs, the Sheep foolishly agree, but the Ram warns that they are not even safe now with the dogs present
The Sheep-dogs volunteer to be sacrificed for peace
